summary: Hold. The spec was written on 2026-10-23 against the parity base. Since then master has landed head-paired FA3 for full layers at batch>1, so as written this change would quietly drop the pairing win on decode_16/32. Whether the kernel can run at all on an H200 at page size 1 and head_dim 64 cannot be checked from this node, and decode has one check left with fused-preattention-triton still in the judge.
justification: A. The motivation numbers are stale. The spec cites SGLang's 623 us at decode_32 full and a 360 us gap, and it argues that FA3 'gathers each 128-byte KV row'. On master (fb07a3bd3aa54baf) the full-layer FA3 kernel is already paired. It reads one 128-byte row per token for both KV heads and costs 152.3 us at decode_16 and 290.2 us at decode_32. That is about 2.26 TB/s at decode_32 over its ~655 MB of KV, whose 4.8 TB/s floor is ~137 us. The kernel the spec would replace is therefore already the access pattern the spec says trtllm fixes. The spec still feeds trtllm an unpaired FP8 [T,16,64] query, so at batch>1 it races an unpaired kernel against paired FA3. Headroom is real but modest. If attention fell from 290 to ~200 us at decode_32 and from 152 to ~100 us at decode_16, the decode_32 load would gain ~7%, the decode_16 load ~4.5%, and the 6-load geomean ~1.9%. Full decode_1 has 18.8 us of FA3 over ~20 MB of KV (floor ~4.3 us), worth roughly 1-2% on that load. The expected directions agree with TASK's weights (full shapes weight 16, sliding and verify are clean controls), but the decode_16/32 'faster' entries are measured against the wrong incumbent. Weakest link: feasibility on this hardware. flashinfer.decode.trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache is the TRT-LLM-gen FMHA path, and its cubins target Blackwell (SM100-class). On SM90 only the XQA backend of newer FlashInfer can serve it, and XQA's supported page sizes (typically >= 16 tokens) and head dims (128 is the common one) probably exclude page size 1 with head_dim 64. Nobody can verify this here: there is no GPU, and FlashInfer is not installed locally. Verifying in the image means spending the decode problem's last check, and the likely result is an import, support or JIT failure rather than a timing. This lineage also has a track record: a hand-written Triton paired-row decode ran 5-7% behind unpaired FA3 and further behind paired FA3, and the stage-2 rewrite was paused for the same reason ('no stage 3 unless a new design beats paired FA3'). The prior that a generic kernel beats paired FA3 at page size 1 is weak.
confounders: fa3-hdim128-head-pairing-batched: direct conflict. It owns the exact call this hypothesis replaces (full layers, batch>1). Swapping in an unpaired trtllm call removes the 7-13% pairing gain on full decode_16/32. A loss there could just be pairing lost, and a gain would understate trtllm against an unpaired FA3. The spec does not say whether the `paired` gate is kept, bypassed or ported to trtllm (feeding trtllm the 128-wide padded query over the [pages,1,1,128] view), so neither outcome is interpretable as written.

fused-preattention-triton (in the judge, not landed): it rewrites the q production that feeds the attention call. If it lands first, it becomes this hypothesis's base and changes what q looks like (dtype, layout, possibly a padded paired query). The spec would have to be rebuilt on it.
marlin-block-m-cap-16, sglang-pipeline-parity-router-hilo-m8: no confound. They touch the MoE and router after attention, and their kernels are identical on every shape this change moves.
interference: No companion fixes this. The problem is not attribution between this change and a sub-change. The spec's base and its incumbent are both out of date, and its feasibility is unknown. An ab-revert of fa3-hdim128-head-pairing-batched would compare trtllm against the old unpaired FA3, which answers a question master no longer asks. With one decode check left, the only sensible next step is a re-mint built on current master (after fused-preattention-triton harvests). The re-mint should state explicitly: (1) the gate (full and q_len==1, with batch>1 also replacing the paired path, or only batch==1, where FA3 is unpaired and 18.8 us); (2) which FlashInfer backend runs on SM90 and its proven support for page_size=1 and head_dim=64, or a paired 128-wide head_dim variant over the existing [pages,1,1,128] view; (3) that cubins come from the image with no runtime download. A batch==1-only variant is the cheapest and cleanest test, because it never competes with pairing and the batch>1 shapes become controls.
rules_flags: Network: FlashInfer's trtllm-gen FMHA path fetches precompiled cubins from a remote cubin repository on first use unless they are bundled in the image (flashinfer-cubin or a populated cache). With no network the run fails, and the pre-run checker rejects submissions that use the network. The implementer must confirm the cubins load from the image.
JIT time: any FlashInfer JIT build counts toward the run's 15-minute budget (the ctx 1048576 test already runs long).
Workspace: FlashInfer needs a workspace buffer, which must be allocated in prepare() or per call, never derived from data. Its zero-initialized semaphore region must stay valid across graph replays.

Host ints: max_seq_len must come from page_table.shape (host int, config-safe), never from seq_lens.max(), which would be a host sync. kv descale must go through bmm1_scale/bmm2_scale as device tensors or config-derived floats; data['k_scale'].item() is not allowed.
No issues with precision (FP8 or BF16 q are both allowed, the cache stays FP8, output is BF16) or with every-key attention (dense decode).
open_questions: Does the lmsysorg/sglang:dev-muse-spark-open image's FlashInfer expose an SM90 backend for trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache (XQA), and does that backend accept page_size=1, head_dim=64, GQA 8 and an FP8 e4m3 KV cache?
Are the trtllm-gen or XQA cubins bundled in the image, or fetched over the network at first use?
Should the re-mint target batch==1 only (unpaired FA3, 18.8 us over a ~4.3 us floor), keep paired FA3 at batch>1, or port the pairing to trtllm with head_dim 128?
Does fused-preattention-triton land first, and if so what q layout does it hand to the attention call?
